name: World's Greatest Stretch
description: The world's greatest stretch is a dynamic compound mobility sequence that combines a hip flexor stretch, thoracic rotation, and hamstring mobilization in a single flowing movement. Starting in a lunge position, the lifter places the same-side hand on the ground while reaching the opposite hand to the ceiling, rotating through the thoracic spine. It is considered one of the most time-efficient warm-up movements as it targets multiple restrictions simultaneously.

execution.starting_position: Begin standing, then step one foot forward into a lunge with the front foot flat and the back leg extended.
execution.setup_instructions: No equipment needed. Use a mat for comfort on the rear knee if needed.
steps: Step 1: Step the right foot forward into a large lunge. Lower the left knee to the floor if needed.
Step 2: Place the right hand on the ground just inside the right foot.
Step 3: Reach the left arm up and open the chest, rotating the thoracic spine toward the ceiling.
Step 4: Hold the rotation for 2–3 breaths, feeling the stretch across the chest, hip flexor, and thoracic spine.
Step 5: Return the left hand to the floor, then stand up and alternate sides.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale into the rotation. Exhale and sink slightly deeper on each breath.
common_mistakes: Rotating from the lower back rather than the thoracic spine
Front knee caving inward — keep it tracking over the second toe
Moving too quickly through the rotation, skipping the breathing component
safety_considerations: If wrist discomfort occurs, make a fist for the supporting hand
Take it slowly — this is a preparatory movement, not a loaded exercise
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Rotate the upper arm as high as the thoracic spine allows. Hips stay square.
execution.tempo_recommendations: 2–3 breaths per side, 5 reps per side, 1–2 rounds.
coaching_cues: Let your eyes follow your hand to encourage the rotation
Press the front knee outward with the inside of your elbow as you rotate
Think tall — reach for the ceiling, not just open to the side
